paragraphs: A man rented a small house in Dublin. He paid €1,600 a month. He says the house was in bad condition from the start.

There were cracks in the walls. A piece of the ceiling fell on his baby son's bed. Later, the cover of the water tank blew away. Birds and dirt got into the water. The water turned brown, and his two small children often got sick.
The landlord knew about the problems but did not fix them. The man stopped paying rent.
A housing board said the landlord did not do the repairs in time. It gave the man €20,000. But he owed rent, so in the end the landlord must pay him only about €1,000.
A Dublin tenant whose son's cot was hit by a piece of falling ceiling has won a case against his landlord at the Residential Tenancies Board, or RTB.

Stephen Russell rented a cottage on Little Strand Street for €1,600 a month from 2020. He said it was in poor condition from the start, and the cracks in the walls and ceilings got worse. In 2024, the cover of the water tank blew off. Dirt and seagulls got into the water, which became brown. The family used it, and their two young children were often sick.

The landlord, Ian Kingsnorth, admitted he knew about the problems from July 2024 but did not fix them. Mr Russell stopped paying rent in February 2025, and a council inspection later found serious problems.

The RTB said the landlord failed to make repairs in a reasonable time and awarded Mr Russell €20,000. However, it took away more than €14,100 for unpaid rent and €4,800 because he would not let the landlord in. In the end, the landlord must pay him €1,032.40.

A Dublin tenant who reported that part of a ceiling had fallen onto his son's cot has been awarded damages by the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB), although most of the sum was cancelled out by unpaid rent.

Stephen Russell began renting a cottage on Little Strand Street in 2020 for €1,600 a month. He told the tribunal that cracks in the walls and ceilings worsened over time. When the cover of the water tank blew away, dirt and gulls contaminated the supply, and the family's two infant children repeatedly needed hospital care.

Landlord Ian Kingsnorth accepted that he had known about the defects since July 2024 and had not dealt with them. After Mr Russell stopped paying rent in 2025, the landlord refused to carry out repairs until the arrears were cleared. A council inspection found "major" breaches of standards.

The tribunal described the tenant's evidence as "very compelling" and awarded him €20,000. However, it deducted rent arrears of over €14,100 and a further €4,800 because he had refused access for an inspection. Mr Kingsnorth must now pay €1,032.40 within 28 days.

Stephen Russell had rented a cottage on Little Strand Street since 2020 at €1,600 a month, and testified that the property was dilapidated from the outset. Once the water tank's cover was dislodged, grime and gulls fouled the supply, and the couple's two infants fell ill repeatedly.

Landlord Ian Kingsnorth conceded he had been aware of the defects since July 2024 yet failed to remedy them. When Mr Russell withheld rent, the landlord refused to undertake repairs until the arrears were settled, a situation he called a "stalemate". A council inspection subsequently identified "major" non-compliance.

Finding the tenant's evidence "very compelling" and an independent contractor's report "damning", the tribunal awarded €20,000. It then offset arrears exceeding €14,100 and docked €4,800 for denying access, leaving Mr Kingsnorth liable for just €1,032.40.

A Dublin tenant who informed the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB) that a section of ceiling had collapsed onto his son's cot has been awarded damages; however, the majority of the sum was offset by accumulated rent arrears.

Stephen Russell had occupied a cottage on Little Strand Street since 2020, paying €1,600 per month, and stated that the property had been in poor repair from the outset. Following the displacement of the water tank's cover, contamination by debris and gulls rendered the supply unsafe, and the family's two infants consequently required repeated medical attention.

Landlord Ian Kingsnorth acknowledged that he had been aware of the defects since July 2024 but had not addressed them. Moreover, once rent payments ceased, he made any repairs contingent upon the arrears being cleared. A subsequent council inspection identified "major" non-compliance with minimum standards.

Although the tribunal regarded the tenant's evidence as "very compelling" and awarded €20,000, it deducted arrears in excess of €14,100, together with €4,800 for the refusal of access. The landlord is therefore obliged to pay only €1,032.40 within 28 days.

summaryHi: डबलिन के किरायेदार को मरम्मत न करने पर हर्जाना मिला, पर बकाया किराया घटाकर लगभग €1,000 ही मिले।
summaryJa: ダブリンの借家人が修繕放置で賠償を勝ち取るも、滞納家賃を差し引き約1000ユーロに。
summaryKo: 더블린 세입자가 수리 방치로 배상을 받았지만 밀린 월세를 빼고 약 1,000유로만 받게 됐다.
summaryZh: 都柏林租客因房東長期不修房屋獲判賠償，但扣除欠租後僅得約一千歐元。
title: Dublin Tenant Wins Damages After Ceiling Falls on Son's Cot
